question: What is the colour code of the dustbin in which non-biodegradable wastes are kept?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Blue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Blue dustbins are specifically designated for non-biodegradable wastes.
 
• Non-biodegradable wastes include items such as plastics, metals, and electronic waste which do not decompose naturally.
 
• Using blue bins helps in the segregation of waste, which is crucial for effective waste management and recycling processes.
 
• Proper segregation of waste into blue bins ensures that non-biodegradable materials can be processed and recycled, reducing environmental pollution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Biodegradable Waste:**

 
 
• These are wastes that cannot be broken down naturally by microorganisms. They include plastics, metals, and chemicals.
 
• Non-biodegradable waste is harmful to the environment as it can persist for years without decomposing.
 
• Such wastes require special handling and recycling processes to minimize their environmental impact.
 
 
 
• **Biodegradable Waste:**
 
 
• This type of waste can be decomposed naturally by microorganisms.
 
• Examples include food waste, garden waste, and paper products.
 
• Biodegradable waste is typically disposed of in green bins and can be composted to produce useful organic matter.
 
 
 
• **Waste Segregation:**
 
 
• Segregation of waste is the process of separating wet waste (biodegradable) and dry waste (non-biodegradable).
 
• Effective waste segregation helps in the efficient recycling and disposal of waste materials.
 
• It reduces the burden on landfills and contributes to environmental conservation.
 
 
 
• **Recycling:**
 
 
• Recycling involves converting waste materials into new products to prevent waste of potentially useful materials.
 
• It reduces the consumption of fresh raw materials, thereby conserving natural resources.
 
• Recycling also helps to reduce energy usage, air and water pollution, and greenhouse gas emissions.
